doc.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998

title: Financial collapse of the band
summary: Leaders paid sidemen from their own pockets, lost $90,000; Sauter went to Baden Baden, Finegan stayed in New York.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Right, I guess. How did the band — did it struggle to stay alive from a financial standpoint?

Yeah. Well it got so bad at one point where the leaders took twenty-five dollars apiece for themselves just to be able to pay the guys in the band. And we didn’t want that. So the band folded. We did just weekends. I left the band, I had left the band, a lot of guys had left the band, and the band did a couple of weekends and that was it. We lost $90,000 in the ‘50s, that was a lot of money then.
And the bill fell on Eddie to pay off, and Finegan.
One of them finally went to Europe, right?
Eddie went to Europe to conduct the Baden Baden, West German Jazz Band. He took a couple of guys from the band with him, including the harpist Blanche Birdsong went and
Sperry Kassman went in percussion and Dave Hildinger went on percussion and piano. And the bass player went.
Finegan stayed where he was. Scuffled in New York.
